A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MIS benchmarking and serialization study. Despite the changed title and organization, their text, tables, figures, equations, and appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original MIS benchmark results on synthetic and real-world graphs, alongside serialization and local-search experiments.

after.justification: Although presented as a position paper, v2 retains original experiments and reports additional RB-graph results and revised PCQO results.

M1.justification: The proposed degree-based serialization algorithm, pseudo-natural LwD serialization, and local-search procedure are retained. Changes concern an evaluated comparator's configuration and the reported serialization repetition count.

E1.justification: v2 adds one graph family through RB-small and RB-large, containing 200–300 and 800–1200 nodes respectively. v1 mentions RB-large only as a source of DiffUCO settings. Existing ER, BA, and real-world coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is retained, but PCQO changes substantively: Appendix B.5 switches from the two-term simplification with γ′=0 to the clique-informed objective with γ′=1. This is a limited revision to one comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix B.5 revises PCQO's tuning protocol: learning rate 0.001 becomes a search over 0.0001, 0.00001, and 0.000001; momentum becomes fixed at 0.9, and the penalty search grid changes. The retained benchmarks otherwise preserve their stated sampling practices and resource limits.

E4.justification: The serialization and local-search analyses are updated, particularly for PCQO. Under its revised configuration, the reported local-search improvement on ER(1000,30) changes from 5.50 to 0.50. The existing analysis questions and LTFT/LwD comparisons remain.

E5.justification: v1 Section 4.2 reports 100 serialization repetitions; v2 Section 5.2 reports 1,000. However, v2 Appendix C.5 still states 100, leaving the actual count internally inconsistent. No confidence intervals, significance tests, or seed reporting are added.

E6.justification: PCQO results are extensively replaced under changed settings: ER(1000,30) changes from 143.00 to 158.63, while BA(10000,5) changes from 4161.88 to 3640.75. Serialization percentages also change. New Table 6 reports RB-large scores of 42.95 for ReduMIS, 39.16 for Deg-Greedy, and 32.55–38.91 for learning-based methods. Most other retained benchmark scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: The MIS definition, serialization formalization, displayed PCQO loss formula, and asymptotic MIS discussion are retained. The conjecture discussion moves from v1 Section 4.4 and Appendix C.5 to v2 Appendix D; no new proof or substantive mathematical revision appears.

C1.justification: v2 reframes the empirical MIS study as a broader position paper advocating changes to CO research, organized around benchmarking deficiencies, learning limitations, and integration of classical heuristics. Classical-solver superiority remains central, while the conjecture challenge disappears from the abstract and main contribution narrative.

C2.justification: Sections 6–7 add substantive arguments about evaluation bias, learning barriers, and circumstances favoring fast AI inference. PCQO is reinterpreted as sharing patterns with stronger solvers rather than uniformly underusing greedy heuristics. Conversely, v1's specific caveat about a prior LwD advantage on excluded very large, sparse graphs is dropped.

D1.justification: Appendix B.5 newly documents PCQO's batch size of 256, 27,000 steps, and 450 steps per batch, alongside its revised tuning recipe. Appendix B.2 adds RB dataset provenance and size ranges. Existing hardware and implementation-source disclosures largely remain.

R1.justification: v2 connects the MIS findings to a broader critique of neural CO through newly cited TSP studies by Joshi et al. and Xia et al., and adds hybrid-method examples from Balcan et al. and Nair et al. These connections support a substantial shift in research positioning beyond the retained MIS literature review.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, and introduction are extensively rewritten. Related work moves earlier, the former conclusion becomes issue–solution and alternative-view sections, and the conjecture discussion moves into a separate appendix. An appendix contents list is also added.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. BA and real-world tables move into the appendix, ER heatmap and serialization panels are combined into Figure 1, and the BA heatmap becomes appendix Figure 2. The conjecture displays are consolidated, and an RB results table is added.

improvement.justification: Using PCQO's full objective with documented tuning makes that comparison more faithful than v1's simplified evaluation. The hard RB benchmarks and practical qualifications in Section 7 add useful evidence and balance. These provide a limited net improvement, tempered by contradictory serialization repetition counts and an unchanged PCQO ratio heatmap in Figure 6 despite revised Table 1 values.
